title: Pre-Analysis — Tailplane Attachment Fitting Interface Standard and Wear Coating
abstract: Pre-analysis of the tailplane attachment fitting standard change, covering the shop refurbishment scheme it overlaps, the box structure change it must not be confused with, the empennage harness that crosses the fitting and the inspection relief the operator has asked for.

sections.objective: Establish what the revised mating face and wear coating standard conflicts with in the existing repair and inspection content, whether the larger gusset fits the installation, and whether the inspection relief the operator wants can be justified before in-service coating data exists.
sections.scope_note: The search covers ATA 55-10 as the primary chapter, including the box structure documents because they share the empennage access and the same shop, and ATA 51-20 for the surface treatment processes the coating change depends on. ATA 92-41 was added after the entity pass returned an empennage wiring sheet in the same zones. Wing, fuselage and systems chapters were excluded; the candidate is confined to the fitting interface.
sections.method_note: Entity linking was seeded from the three part numbers, the drawing and the two stabiliser access zones. The zones alone returned the empennage harness sheet, which no one in the review had associated with a fitting change. Similarity was run over the fretting and load redistribution narrative and returned the box structure stiffener change, which shares no part number, no drawing and no zone with the candidate but describes the same structure being changed for the same class of reason two bays away.
sections.findings_summary: Seven items are confirmed and one is blocking. The blocking item is the shop refurbishment scheme: it already blends and re-protects the mating faces to a specification, and the candidate changes the coating those faces receive. A fitting refurbished under the current scheme and then re-coated under the candidate would have an undefined stack of two schemes, and the shop has no instruction for which one governs. The stiffener extension change is the item similarity found: same structure, same shop visit, same fatigue-driven justification, and no shared identifier at all — the two are being progressed by different offices and neither had the other on its list. The empennage harness sheet crosses the fitting region and its support brackets are dimensioned from the fitting datum, so a larger gusset bearing face moves them even though no wire changes. The attachment inspection task carries the interval the operator wants relieved, and the splice repair scheme shares the shop and the access. The retrofit bulletin for the box structure work states that the stabiliser is interchangeable between airframes after embodiment, which the candidate must not break. The parts figure needs the fitting and gusset split by effectivity.
sections.next_steps: Agree with the repair design owner which coating scheme governs a refurbished fitting. Bring the stiffener extension owner into the review before either change is frozen. Measure the gusset bearing face against the harness bracket positions. Tell the operator that inspection relief cannot be granted before in-service coating data exists, and offer a data collection scheme instead.

similarity_seeds: bright marks on a mating face found earlier than the maintenance programme assumes
load turning into the structure sooner than the substantiation predicted

tasks.title: Search the stabiliser structure family on the entity seeds
Search for comparable early structural findings on other chapters
Reconcile the coating scheme with the shop refurbishment
Measure the gusset bearing face against the harness bracket positions
Prepare the data collection scheme offered instead of inspection relief

expected_findings.rationale: The refurbishment scheme blends the mating face and applies a surface treatment and wear coating to a specification of its own. The candidate changes that specification at build. A fitting refurbished under the existing scheme and then re-coated under the candidate carries two schemes with no defined interaction, and the shop has no rule for which governs.
expected_findings.resolution: Agree one governing specification with repair design and re-issue the refurbishment scheme in the same package as the modification.

evidence.similarity_note: Both describe the same stabiliser being changed because load or wear appears earlier than the substantiation assumed, one at the upper panel splice and one at the attachment fittings. They share no part number, no drawing, no zone and no functional item number, and they use different vocabulary throughout — stiffener run and splice plate against mating face and wear coating.

expected_findings.rationale: Both changes are embodied with the stabiliser removed, in the same shop, on overlapping aircraft, and both are justified by structure behaving earlier than predicted. They are being progressed by different offices and neither appears on the other's list. Embodying them at separate shop visits would cost the operator a second stabiliser removal.
expected_findings.resolution: Bring both owners into one review and decide whether the two are offered as a single shop package.

expected_findings.rationale: The empennage harness runs through both stabiliser access zones and its support brackets are dimensioned from the fitting datum rather than from the frame, precisely because the fitting is the feature that does not move. A larger gusset bearing face moves them, and the sheet's stated 25 millimetre clearance to the fitting bearing face may not be met at the travel limits.
expected_findings.resolution: Measure the clearance with the new gusset at both travel limits and reissue the sheet if the bracket positions change.

expected_findings.rationale: The stabiliser inspection task is the vehicle for any interval change, and the operator's request is for relief from the refurbishment scope at heavy check. The task cannot be relieved before coating performance data exists, and the request has to be answered in the task rather than in the modification.
expected_findings.resolution: Keep the current interval, add a data recording step and revisit the interval after two heavy checks on coated fittings.

expected_findings.rationale: The splice region crack repair is an interim scheme valid for a limited number of cycles and is embodied in the same shop with the stabiliser off. An aircraft carrying it would have to have the shop repair and the fitting work planned together, or it will make two visits.
expected_findings.resolution: Flag the interim repair population and plan the fitting work into the same shop visit.

evidence.similarity_note: Both documents describe shop work on the same stabiliser with the same access and the same interchangeability claim, in different words and with no shared identifier.

expected_findings.rationale: The box structure bulletin states that the stabiliser remains interchangeable between airframes after embodiment. The candidate changes the fitting interface standard, and if a coated fitting cannot be mated to an uncoated airframe interface that statement stops being true for aircraft carrying both.
expected_findings.resolution: Confirm interchangeability across mixed coating standards and restate it in both documents.

expected_findings.rationale: The stabiliser figure carries the box structure items split by effectivity but shows no attachment fitting items at all, because they have never changed. The candidate replaces the aft fitting and the gusset, so the figure needs new items and a new effectivity split.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the fitting and gusset items to the figure with their effectivity when the modification is released.

expected_non_findings.reason: Surfaces high on similarity because it is also a structural repair scheme about a crack at a fitting interface with bore and land limits, in very similar language. It is a cabin window intercostal, shares no part number, no zone and no shop process with the candidate.

Returned because it is also about replacing case-by-case engineering judgement with a published standard, and it uses the same vocabulary of limits, blends and acceptance. It is a lower shell doubler family with no empennage content and no shared identifier.

type_data.conclusion: Not yet issued. The work order is on hold pending the harness bracket measurement, which cannot be done until an aircraft with the new gusset geometry is available.
